correctness.rationale: At a word with x rotations and even positive y reflections, the rotation exponent is x−2j mod n for any 0≤j≤x by placement in alternating reflection gaps. Hence identity counts are: y=0 iff n|x; odd y never; positive even y with n even iff x even; with n odd iff x even or x≥n. Myhill–Nerode equivalence of commutative language prefixes is exactly equality of these shifted (x+u,y+v) predicates. For even n≥4, y=0 yields n congruence classes and y>0 yields four disjoint parity classes, each separated with specified suffixes; n=2 merges to four parity classes. For odd n≥3, the y=0 classes are n−1 short-tail states and n residue-cycle states, and y>0 gives 2n classes from y-parity and saturation min(x,n−1). Long a-suffixes/b² test separate the families. Thus 4n−1; original Cayley DFA is 2n by positive inverses. No experimental range is presented as proof. Independent from-scratch group-product dynamic programming found 2290 agreement triples for n=2..26, and independently enumerated pairwise distinguishable suffix signatures with b-suffix lengths 0,1,2 for all quotient witnesses n=2..54, recovering all claimed state counts. value.rationale: This is a complete all-n exact state-complexity classification for a canonical, naturally given group identity language, with an explicit structural parity transition in the direction of complexity change. Group-theoretic parity and eventual saturation explain n+4 versus 4n−1; it is not a single arbitrary finite computation, mere parameter substitution, or direct consequence of the published generic regularity bounds. It supplies reusable explicit minimal right-quotient descriptions for a familiar nonabelian finite-group family. The limited alphabet and identity acceptance are essential scope restrictions, not hidden generalizations.

final_claim: For D_n=<a,b | a^n=b²=1, bab=a^{-1}> and the positive identity word language over {a,b}, the commutative closure has exactly 4 states for n=2, n+4 states for even n≥4, and 4n−1 states for odd n≥3, whereas the original group identity language has 2n complete-DFA states.
limitations: Only positive generators a,b with a^n=b²=1 and bab=a^{-1}, identity acceptance and minimal complete DFAs.
No claim about other accepting subsets, generating alphabets, NDFA state complexity or arbitrary finite groups.
Finite independently checked n=2..54 cannot prove all-n; proof is symbolic and group-theoretic.
